guide:
You write Sceliph AssemblyIR JSON. Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else: {"view":{"azimuthDeg":number,"elevationDeg":number},"assembly":AssemblyIR}.
AssemblyIR: {"schema":"morphloom.assembly/0.1","name":string,"units":"mm","components":[component,...]}
component: {"id":string,"name":string,"category":one of "enclosure","display","logic","power","camera","audio","radio","mechanical","interconnect","materialName":string,"detail":string,"geometry":geometry,"position":[x,y,z] (optional, mm, centre of the part),"rotation":[rx,ry,rz] (optional, radians, XYZ Euler),"material":{"color":"#rrggbb","roughness":0..1 (optional),"metalness":0..1 (optional)}}
World: millimetres, Y is up, the floor is y = 0. Each geometry is centred on the component position.
geometry options:
- {"op":"roundedBox","size":[x,y,z],"radius":r}  (r at most 0.4 x the smallest size)
- {"op":"cylinder","radiusTop":r1,"radiusBottom":r2,"depth":h,"radialSegments":32}  (axis along Y, height h)
- {"op":"sphere","radius":r}
- {"op":"torus","radius":R,"tube":t}  (ring lies in the XY plane; its axis is Z; outer diameter 2(R+t); rotate it for other planes)
- {"op":"tube","points":[[x,y,z],...],"radius":r}  (swept circle along a smooth curve through the points, relative to the component position; a straight rod or brace needs exactly two points, otherwise the curve bends)
- {"op":"lathe","profile":[[r,y],...],"segments":48}  (profile radius r >= 0 at height y, relative to the component position, revolved about the vertical Y axis; for vases, lamp bases, turned legs, shades)
- {"op":"extrude","points":[[x,y],...],"depth":d}  (closed outline in the X-Y plane relative to the component position, extruded along Z by d and centred on it; for shaped panels, brackets, cut-out legs)
Choose the components yourself: 2 to 16 meaningful rigid parts (top, legs, drawer fronts, shade, base, ...), each with a short unique id.
You are modelling the product in a catalog photograph whose background has been removed. The user states the overall height from the product listing; make the model exactly that tall and derive every other size and placement from the photo in proportion to it.
Put the object on the floor (lowest point at y = 0) and model only the object, not the floor or background.
"view" is your estimate of where the photo was taken from, relative to your own model: azimuthDeg 0 means the camera looks at the model's +Z side (from +Z toward -Z); positive azimuth moves the camera toward +X (azimuth 90 = camera on the +X side). elevationDeg is the camera height angle above the horizontal (0 = level, 90 = straight down).
Give every component an explicit "position".

a1: The product listing gives its overall height as {height} mm.
a2: The second photo shows the same product from the same camera after the turntable turned it a quarter turn (90 degrees) about the vertical axis; both photos use the same zoom, so their pixel scales match. Use it for the depth and the hidden sides. "view" refers to the first photo.
The product listing gives its overall height as {height} mm.

note: 9b test protocol. Identical to protocol-dev.json except note and preregistration; frozen after the 10-item dev pass and before any test item was run or viewed.

preregistration.registered: 2026-10-27, after dev-sonnet (10 slice-8 dev items, 1 repeat) and before any test call
preregistration.selection: benchmarks/oss-integration-20261026/abo-multiview/selection.json (continued seeded order after the 55 slice-8 items; strata thin = LAMP, LIGHT_FIXTURE, ELECTRIC_FAN; test 24 thin + 12 other)

replacements.rule: a test item whose product is a colour or size variant of a slice-8 item (same product line and design, decided from names and mesh metadata only, before any image) is replaced by the next reserve item of the same stratum

replaced.B07GFLD8VP: B07HSCYS4C (Inari desk colour variant of slice-8 dev B07GFFQZRQ)
replaced.B082XLMW6G: B082JH9VWG (Rivet fan colour variant of slice-8 test B082XMF2RV)
replaced.B082XMRGZG: B0825D147R (Rivet fan, same 52in body as B082XMF2RV)
replaced.B07XGQ9QJF: B0828FFDWG (4-inch variant of slice-8 reserve 6-inch table fan B07XJB28C7)

preregistration.analysis: scripts/abo-multiview-summary.ts (items averaged over repeats; bootstrap over items, seed 20261027)
criteria: footprint-gain: thin, median paired (a2 - a1) footprint error < 0 and 95% CI upper < 0
no-shape-loss: thin, median paired (a2 - a1) Chamfer/diag <= +0.001
beats-hull: all, median paired (a2 - b2) Chamfer/diag < 0 and 95% CI upper < 0
absolute-footprint: thin, a2 footprint error median <= 10%
preregistration.devObservation: dev (mostly 3/4 views, 1 repeat): a2 footprint better on 3, worse on 6 of 10, mostly by small amounts; prediction: footprint-gain likely fails
